history.text:
The question is whether P9's compatibility objection requires any change to an account of global availability, and if so what P7's target distinction identifies as being questioned. The frozen material supplies P7 on criticism targets, P9 on local alternatives and global bounds with the correlation loss objection, and a prior E009 criticism whose standing is explicitly unendorsed, concerning a Lean expression rather than P7 or P9 themselves. Nothing in the packet asserts that the missing constraint exists. I will build a small construction that connects the two, mark exactly which parts are the source's and which are mine, and name the observation or interpretation that would matter.

What P9 supplies, taken at face value, is: per-booking reservations are quantities of greatest-revision active holds, or zero, or unresolved among tied greatest-revision active holds; global availability is capacity minus the sum; the sum is not well-defined when there are unresolved alternatives; per-booking minimum and maximum give a global interval; intervals lose correlations because a booking-A high alternative may be incompatible with a booking-B high alternative if they share an unnamed physical resource; the snapshot does not name physical resources, so this incompatibility is invisible; a conjecture is that the snapshot is under-specified for any real warehouse; a criticism is that exposing alternatives without a resolution policy pushes the problem downstream.

What P7 supplies, taken at face value, is: criticism targets can be a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful; "this snapshot is inconsistent" can mean at least three different things (two active greatest-revision holds for one booking; total reservations exceeding capacity; logical time behind an expected expiry); a conjecture that many apparent availability disagreements are disagreements about targets; a criticism of the supersession rule differs from a criticism of a high-revision implausible-quantity record; preserving the distinction matters because one can reject a rule while accepting data, or accept a rule while rejecting data.

I will not restate these. The construction below adds an organization that neither passage contains by itself.

## 1. The distinction I add: bound-arithmetic target vs bound-correspondence target

P9 treats the correlation objection as if it bears on the availability calculation. Read literally, the sentence "intervals lose correlations" points at the interval representation, i.e., at the pair (lower bound, upper bound) of the availability number. But the sentence continues: the incompatibility is "invisible" because the snapshot does not name physical resources. That continuation names a missing constraint, not a numerical error. The two halves of P9's objection are therefore already doing different work, but P9 does not separate them and P7 does not name them.

I propose that the correlation objection actually splits P7's "snapshot-as-a-whole" target into two further targets:

- **Bound-arithmetic target.** The claim that the reported interval [capacity minus sum of per-booking maxima, capacity minus sum of per-booking minima] is the correct availability interval for this snapshot. This target is a claim about arithmetic given per-booking possibility sets.
- **Bound-correspondence target.** The claim that the reported interval corresponds to the set of actually realizable global configurations. This target is a claim about the relation between the snapshot's data and an unstated availability-relevant structure.

Under this split, the correlation objection is not a criticism of the availability account's arithmetic. The arithmetic can be correct — capacity minus maxima is indeed a lower bound over the product of per-booking possibility sets — while the correspondence claim fails whenever the product set is not the realizable set. Booking A's high alternative can co-occur with booking B's high alternative in the product set and not co-occur in the warehouse. So the interval can be arithmetically right and correspondentially wrong. P7's distinction between "criticizing a rule" and "criticizing data" does not by itself name this split, because both halves of the correlation objection target the snapshot as a whole rather than any rule or record. The additional distinction is between two sub-targets of the same snapshot-level claim, distinguished by whether the claim is internal to the arithmetic or external to the modeled structure.

This distinction is mine. Nothing in P7 or P9 says that "snapshot-as-a-whole" contains these two sub-targets. P9's own sentence "intervals lose correlations" would, read alone, suggest the objection is about intervals; my reading redirects it to a gap between modeled and realizable joint configurations.

## 2. Why the compatibility objection does not force a change to the arithmetic account

P9's own framing makes the compatibility a conditional: "might be incompatible." The physical resource is "not named in the snapshot." Given those two facts, the claim "the interval is the best available bound" is not refuted. The claim "the interval corresponds to what can actually happen" is refuted only under the additional premise that a resource constraint exists that the snapshot does not record. Neither premise is in the packet.

So my proposed account is:

- No change is required to the availability arithmetic if "availability" is read as the interval over the product of per-booking possibility sets. That interval is a well-defined, arithmetically correct summary of the snapshot's per-booking alternatives.
- A change is required to any claim that this interval characterizes what the warehouse can actually do. If the pre-theoretic question is "how much can be promised without violating capacity," and if capacity is only one of several shared constraints, then the interval is a projection of a set the snapshot does not determine.

This is not a new language component. It is a re-description of what "availability" is a name for: the bound on a modeled product set, not the bound on a physical possibility set. The distinction between the two names is what the correlation objection actually forces. P9 slips between them ("availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected" earlier, "interval" later), and P7's "snapshot-as-a-whole" target is not fine-grained enough to catch the slip.

I am not installing a repair. I am proposing that the correlation objection is best classified, in P7's sense, as a criticism of the snapshot-as-a-whole that specifically fails the correspondence half and leaves the arithmetic half alone. If this is right, then the E009 criticism's preoccupation with whether WHL's `availability_lower_bound` and `availability_upper_bound` are named backwards is addressing the arithmetic half, not the correspondence half. P9's correlation objection would survive any repair of those names.

## 3. Criticism of the proposal

**Objection 1 — Is the split real or verbal?** One could say the arithmetic claim just is the correspondence claim under a different description, since "capacity minus maxima" is only meaningful as a bound on a set. Reply: the two come apart when the per-booking possibility sets are not the projections of any joint possibility set. Then "capacity minus maxima" is a well-defined number describable without reference to any joint set, and it can be reported even when no joint set exists. That is exactly the case P9 describes.

**Objection 2 — Does the split do new work, or just rename?** It changes what a reader should look at. Under P9's framing as written, a reader who rejects the interval is invited to look at the interval machinery. Under my split, a reader who rejects the interval may need to look at whether the snapshot is being asked a question it cannot answer. The E009 criticism's repairs to WHL's naming do not address the latter. That is new work.

**Objection 3 — Is calling this a "target" rather than a "reading" consistent with P7?** P7 names snapshot-as-a-whole as a target; my split subdivides that target rather than introducing a new kind of object. If someone thinks P7's list of targets is exhaustive and indivisible, the split is a disagreement with P7's taxonomy, not with P9's objection. I flag this rather than resolve it.

**Objection 4 — Doesn't the correspondence failure only matter if you care about physical realizability?** Yes. The split only matters for a reader whose question is about the warehouse rather than about the snapshot. P9 itself does not stipulate that question. The criticism's scope is narrower than P9's phrasing suggests. This is a partial defense of the original framing.

## 4. What observation or interpretation would matter

The split is decided by whether one can exhibit a snapshot and an unstated resource model where the per-booking possibility sets have a product set strictly larger than the realizable set. P9's example (bookings A and B with high alternatives sharing an unnamed resource) is an illustration, not a case. A demonstration would require: a named resource not modeled by capacity, per-booking possibility sets from the snapshot, and at least one joint configuration in the product set that violates the resource. Without such a demonstration, the split is a distinction in search of a case.

Alternatively, the split fails if "availability" is stipulated to range only over the modeled product set. Then no correspondence claim is being made, and P9's phrasing "intervals lose correlations" is simply an admission about the interval representation rather than a criticism of a further claim. Under that stipulation, my split collapses back into the arithmetic half.

So the discriminating interpretation is: does any account of "availability" for this snapshot implicitly claim correspondence with a realizable joint set, or is the name reserved for a summary over the product set? P7 does not decide this; P9 does not decide it. The packet supplies the demand for the distinction, not its resolution.

## 5. Relationship of the E009 criticism to this construction

The E009 criticism is explicitly unendorsed. Its main targets (WHL's naming backwards for availability bounds, `expired_deletes_rule` not actually deleting, `Commitment := Prop` losing account-relativity, revision having no totality) are about the Lean layer's internal coherence and about whether WHL can express P7's target list. Under my split, those are defects of the arithmetic-side formalization and of the target-list formalization. They do not engage P9's correspondence-side objection, because WHL has no primitive for joint realizability beyond the capacity sum. The E009 criticism actually notes this: "intervals lose correlations… WHL cannot represent non-convex sets or correlations across bookings… Proposed repair: add a resource model or a possible-worlds set. Not installed." That proposed repair names the correspondence side, but E009 treats it as one item in a list rather than as the item that survives every repair of the arithmetic side. My construction moves it to the front and says which half of P9 it belongs to.

history.text:
The construction is coherent as an episode, but it contains at least one specific defect that I think is established by the frozen material rather than merely proposed. The defect is not in P7, P9, or the E009 criticism. It is in the construct's central claim that P9's correlation objection "splits" the snapshot-as-a-whole target into a bound-arithmetic target and a bound-correspondence target. That split is not a distinction the source's target taxonomy can carry without a change the construct does not acknowledge, and the construct's own framing of the split quietly imports a standpoint — realizability under an unstated resource model — that P7 lists separately from the snapshot-as-a-whole target.

The relevant P7 text is:

> "One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful."

The list has five items, and the last three are different *types* of thing: a booking's history is a temporal sequence of records, the snapshot as a whole is the current aggregate, and "the assumption that logical time is meaningful" is neither a record nor an aggregate but a background presupposition. P9's correlation objection concerns "a physical resource not named in the snapshot." That unnamed resource is not a record, not a booking's history, not the snapshot as a whole, and not the meaningfulness of logical time. It is a presupposition about the modeled world — specifically, that capacity is the only relevant shared constraint. The construct's "bound-correspondence target" is therefore best understood, in P7's own taxonomy, as a criticism of a *source assumption* (compare P7's later remark: "one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late"), not as a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target.

The construct does not say this. Instead it asserts:

> "I propose that the correlation objection actually splits P7's 'snapshot-as-a-whole' target into two further targets…"

That is a claim about P7's taxonomy that P7's taxonomy does not support. P7's list is exhaustive in the local sense that it names the kinds of things a criticism can address; adding a "bound-correspondence target" inside "snapshot-as-a-whole" attributes to the snapshot an external-comparison component that P7 assigns, if anywhere, to source assumptions. The construct's own Objection 3 half-acknowledges this:

> "If someone thinks P7's list of targets is exhaustive and indivisible, the split is a disagreement with P7's taxonomy, not with P9's objection."

But the construct then declines to resolve the flag, and elsewhere it proceeds as if the split were a reading of P7 rather than a revision of it. That is the specific defect: an unsupported re-classification of a source target, presented as a subdivision rather than as a proposed amendment.

The distinction matters because the two readings of the correlation objection give different answers to the construct's guiding question. Under the re-classification reading, P9's objection does not force any change to a P7-respecting account of global availability *as an account of the snapshot*; it forces a change to an account of what the snapshot is being used to describe, which P7's target list already marks as a distinct target ("the assumption that logical time is meaningful" — and, by extension, other source assumptions). Under the subdivision reading, the objection falls inside the availability account itself, and some change to that account is required. The construct switches between these readings. It says, correctly under the re-classification reading:

> "No change is required to the availability arithmetic if 'availability' is read as the interval over the product of per-booking possibility sets."

And it also says, under the subdivision reading:

> "A change is required to any claim that this interval characterizes what the warehouse can actually do."

Both sentences can be true, but they answer different questions, and the construct treats them as one account rather than two. The P7-respecting way to keep both is to say that the correlation objection targets a *source assumption about what the snapshot models*, not the availability account's internal consistency. P7 already provides the slot; the construct does not use it.

A second, smaller defect compounds the first. The E009 criticism, on the construct's reading, "does not engage P9's correspondence-side objection, because WHL has no primitive for joint realizability beyond the capacity sum." That is accurate as far as it goes, but the construct then says:

> "The E009 criticism actually notes this… That proposed repair names the correspondence side, but E009 treats it as one item in a list rather than as the item that survives every repair of the arithmetic side. My construction moves it to the front and says which half of P9 it belongs to."

"Which half of P9 it belongs to" is exactly the question the construct has not settled, because it has not decided whether the correspondence side is a target inside the availability account or a source assumption outside it. So the construct claims to have moved the E009 item to the front and assigned it, when in fact it has moved it to the front and left its assignment to P7's taxonomy open. That is not an error in the E009 criticism; it is an unfinished move in the construction.

I want to be careful about what I am and am not claiming. I am not claiming that the construct's split is false, or that a revised target taxonomy would be unwarranted. The construct's own Objection 4 ("Doesn't the correspondence failure only matter if you care about physical realizability? Yes.") is a candid acknowledgment that the split's relevance depends on a stipulated question. What I am claiming is narrower and I think established by the sources: the split is not a reading of P7's target list, because P7 already supplies a target for external presuppositions about what the snapshot models, and the construct does not notice this. Presenting the split as a subdivision of "snapshot-as-a-whole" loses the distinction P7 was careful to draw between criticizing the object and criticizing the assumption under which the object is read. That is a lost distinction, not a mere stylistic choice.

A rival reading is available that keeps the construct intact: perhaps by "snapshot as a whole" P7 meant something broad enough to include the snapshot's implicit modeling commitments, so that the split is genuinely internal to that target. If so, the construct's proposal is compatible with P7 and my criticism fails. The construct does not supply textual support for this broader reading, and P7's separate mention of "the assumption that logical time is meaningful" weighs against it. I note this as an open interpretive question rather than as a settled defect, but I do think the burden falls on the broader reading, since P7's list is otherwise composed of items at clearly different levels of abstraction, and the level occupied by "the assumption that…" is the natural home for "the assumption that capacity is the only shared constraint."

One further point, since the carrier is unconstrained prose and I should not over-formalize: the construct's insistence that "this is not a new language component" is defensible if and only if the split is read as a re-description of what "availability" names. But whether an account of global availability implicitly claims correspondence is not something the account can settle by re-description alone; it depends on what downstream consumers of the account are entitled to infer. P9's criticism — "exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently" — is precisely about this entitlement, and the construct's split does not touch it. So even on the construct's own reading, the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection pull in different directions: the first can be absorbed by re-description, the second cannot. The construct presents them as if they belonged to the same layer. That, too, is a small but specific loss of distinction, and it is one the frozen packet already contains in P9.

Bottom line: the construction adds a useful distinction and connects P7 and P9 in a way neither contains alone. But its central move — treating the bound-correspondence target as an internal subdivision of P7's snapshot-as-a-whole target — is not supported by P7's own target list, which already contains a distinct slot for assumptions about what the snapshot models. Either the construct should present the split as a proposed amendment to P7's taxonomy, or it should re-locate the correspondence side to the source-assumption target. As written, it does neither, and that is a defect established by the frozen material rather than merely conjectured.

history.text:
# Successor to the construct, with the criticism carried

I am answering the criticism on its own terms: only where the substantive reason warrants a change do I revise; otherwise I preserve the construct and explain why the objection does not establish the defect. I keep the frozen P7 excerpt, the frozen P9 excerpt, the operator contract, the construct occurrence, and the criticism occurrence as distinct historical occurrences; nothing here is installed in the frozen carrier. The proposed successor below is a separate proposed object.

## 1. What I accept from the criticism

The criticism makes one specific, textual claim I think is established by the frozen material rather than merely proposed. P7's target list runs:

> "One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful."

The last item is not a record, a history, or an aggregate. It is a background presupposition under which the other items are read. P9's correlation objection concerns "a physical resource not named in the snapshot" — that is, a presupposition about which shared constraints the snapshot is taken to model, not a further fact about the snapshot's contents. So the construct's "bound-correspondence target" has a better home in P7's taxonomy as a criticism of a *source assumption* than as a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target. The construct said:

> "I propose that the correlation objection actually splits P7's 'snapshot-as-a-whole' target into two further targets…"

and did not notice that P7 already supplies a distinct slot for assumptions about what the snapshot models. That is a real defect, not a stylistic choice: it collapses a distinction P7 was careful to draw.

I also accept the smaller follow-on: when the construct says its construction "moves [the E009 item] to the front and says which half of P9 it belongs to," it has not yet settled which half, because it has not yet settled whether the correspondence side is a target inside the availability account or a source assumption outside it. That is an unfinished move, and the criticism correctly names it.

And I accept the third observation: P9's downstream-resolution criticism ("exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently") and P9's correlation objection do not belong to the same layer. The first is about entitlement of downstream consumers; the second is about correspondence between the modeled interval and a realizable joint set. The construct's re-description reply — "this is not a new language component… availability names the interval over the product of per-booking possibility sets" — can absorb the correlation objection under a stipulation, but it does not absorb the downstream-resolution objection. Presenting them as one layer loses that distinction.

## 2. What I do not accept, and why

The criticism's strongest move is its re-location of the correspondence side to the source-assumption slot. I accept that as the better reading, but I do not accept the implication that this makes the construct's *guiding question* moot, or that the construct's arithmetic-side / correspondence-side split is therefore unsupported. The criticism's own Objection 3, restated, says P7's list may be exhaustive in a local sense; the construct flagged exactly that and declined to resolve it. The criticism takes the flag and treats it as an unacknowledged revision. It is acknowledged. The construct says:

> "If someone thinks P7's list of targets is exhaustive and indivisible, the split is a disagreement with P7's taxonomy, not with P9's objection. I flag this rather than resolve it."

So the defect is not that the construct proceeded as if the split were a reading of P7. The defect is that the construct, having flagged the issue, continued to use the phrase "subdivision of snapshot-as-a-whole" in later sections as if the flag had been resolved in favor of the subdivision reading. I accept *that* — the inconsistency between the flag and later usage. I do not accept that the split itself is unsupported, only that its *classification* was left ambiguous.

On the second defect, I partially accept. The construct says E009 "does not engage P9's correspondence-side objection, because WHL has no primitive for joint realizability beyond the capacity sum." That is accurate. The criticism's point that "which half of P9 it belongs to is exactly the question the construct has not settled" is fair as stated, but the construct's sentence is also readable as an observation that the E009 item *can* be assigned either way depending on the reading — and that this is itself the open question. The construct could have been clearer. I accept the clarification, not the charge of error.

On the third point — the different direction of the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection — I accept it as a genuine improvement, not as a defect in the construct. The construct did not say they were the same layer; it discussed them in adjacent sections and treated both as elements of P9. But the criticism sharpens the distinction, and I incorporate that sharpening below.

## 3. The successor: re-classification, not subdivision

The successor preserves the construct's substantive split between bound-arithmetic and bound-correspondence readings of the correlation objection. It changes the classification of the second half, and it distinguishes the two P9 objections by layer.

**Successor claim S1 (re-classification).** The bound-arithmetic target is a criticism of a reconstruction rule — specifically, of the rule that the availability interval for a snapshot is [capacity − Σ per-booking maximum, capacity − Σ per-booking minimum], read as an arithmetic claim over the product of per-booking possibility sets. The bound-correspondence target is not a subdivision of the snapshot-as-a-whole target; it is a criticism of a source assumption, namely the assumption that capacity is the only shared constraint that bears on joint realizability. This places the correspondence side in the slot P7 already provides ("the assumption that logical time is meaningful" and, by extension, other source assumptions about what the snapshot models), rather than manufacturing a new sub-target inside "snapshot as a whole."

**Successor claim S2 (layered objections).** P9's correlation objection and P9's downstream-resolution objection are criticisms at different layers, with different scope:

- The correlation objection can be absorbed by stipulation: if "availability" names the interval over the modeled product set, no correspondence claim is made, and no change to the arithmetic is required. The objection then only bites if someone claims the interval characterizes the warehouse, not the model. Under P7's taxonomy, the claim that it characterizes the warehouse is a claim about a source assumption, not about the availability account's internal arithmetic.
- The downstream-resolution objection cannot be absorbed by stipulation. It is a criticism of the practice of exposing unresolved alternatives without a resolution policy, and it concerns the entitlement of consumers to infer commitments from the exposure. Under P7's taxonomy, it targets the snapshot-as-a-whole as a *presentation*, not as a model, and it does not reduce to the correlation objection.

**Successor claim S3 (preserved construct content).** The following construct claims are preserved without change, because the criticism does not establish a defect in them:

- The distinction between the two halves of P9's correlation objection (arithmetic vs correspondence).
- The observation that the arithmetic can be correct while a correspondence claim fails, because the per-booking possibility sets need not be projections of any joint possibility set.
- The candid acknowledgment that the correspondence failure only matters if a reader cares about physical realizability, and that P9's example is an illustration rather than a case.
- The observation that E009's proposed repair "add resource model or possible-worlds set" names the correspondence side, and that E009 treats it as one item in a list.
- The observation that P9's correlation objection would survive any repair of WHL's availability-bound naming.

**Successor claim S4 (what remains an open interpretive question).** Whether P7's "snapshot as a whole" was meant broadly enough to include the snapshot's implicit modeling commitments. The construct flagged this; the criticism notes it; the successor leaves it unresolved and says so. The successor's re-classification (S1) is a proposed reading, not a stipulation about P7's intent.

## 4. Answering the guiding question under the successor

The contract's guiding question is: does P9's compatibility objection require any change to an account of global availability, and if so what is being questioned in P7's sense?

Under the successor:

- **No change to the availability arithmetic** is required by the correlation objection alone. The arithmetic over the modeled product set is well-defined and can be reported. This is preserved from the construct.
- **A change to a claim about correspondence** is required only if the account is read as claiming that the interval characterizes the warehouse. Under P7's taxonomy, this is not a criticism of the availability rule; it is a criticism of a source assumption about what the snapshot models.
- **A change to the availability account's presentation** may be required by the downstream-resolution objection, but that objection is about entitlement, not about arithmetic, and it is not settled by the correlation objection. This is the layered-objections point (S2) the construct did not draw.

So the successor's answer to the guiding question is: the compatibility objection is a criticism of a source assumption, not of the availability account's internal arithmetic. Under the arithmetic-side reading, it changes nothing in the account. Under the correspondence-side reading, it changes which claim is being made, not how the arithmetic is done. The E009 criticism's repairs to WHL's naming address the arithmetic side and do not engage either the correspondence side or the downstream-resolution side. The E009 criticism's proposed repair "add a resource model or possible-worlds set" names the correspondence side but does not decide whether it belongs to the availability account or to a source assumption, and the E009 criticism does not raise the downstream-resolution objection at all.

## 5. What remains protected after the successor

The contract's protected distinctions are preserved and their locations named:

- **Criticizing a rule vs. criticizing its records**: preserved. In the successor's classification, the arithmetic side is a criticism of a rule (the interval rule); the source-assumption side is not a criticism of a record.
- **Different combinations of accepting/rejecting rule and data**: preserved, and now located. Rejecting the arithmetic rule while accepting the records is a rule criticism. Accepting the arithmetic rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late is a data criticism. The correspondence claim is neither: it is a claim about what the snapshot models.
- **Cross-booking incompatibility as conditional possibility, not observation**: preserved. P9 says "might be incompatible"; the successor's correspondence side is conditional on the same premise.
- **Local alternatives, aggregation, bounds, correlation objections as different roles**: preserved with the layering (S2). Local alternatives drive the per-booking possibility set; aggregation produces the interval; the correlation objection is the claim that the interval may not correspond; the downstream-resolution objection is the claim that exposure without policy shifts the problem.
- **Exposing alternatives vs. objecting to downstream resolution as disputed positions**: preserved. The successor does not resolve the dispute; it locates it at a different layer from the correlation objection.
- **No endorsement of the missing constraint**: preserved. The successor's correspondence side is conditional on a premise the packet does not assert.

## 6. What observation or interpretation would matter, under the successor

The successor's S1 and S2 are decided by observation in the same way the construct's split was:

- S1 (re-classification) is decided by textual reading of P7. Under the broad reading of "snapshot as a whole," the construct's original subdivision holds and the successor's re-classification fails. Under the narrow reading, the successor's re-classification holds. The successor notes this (S4) rather than resolving it.
- S2 (layering) is decided by whether the correlation objection and the downstream-resolution objection can be separated. If someone argues they are the same objection under different descriptions, S2 fails. The construct's argument was that they belong to adjacent sections of P9; the criticism sharpened this by showing they pull in different directions (one absorbable by stipulation, one not). The successor adopts the sharpening.

The further observation that would settle the original split remains the same: a snapshot plus an unstated resource model where the per-booking possibility sets have a product set strictly larger than the realizable set. Without such a case, the correspondence side is a distinction in search of an instance. Under the successor's re-classification, this observation would settle a claim about a source assumption, not a claim about the availability account's internal coherence — which is what the criticism said the construct should have noticed.

## 7. What I am not claiming

I am not claiming that the successor's re-classification is forced by P7. It is a proposed reading, and the broad reading remains open. I am not claiming that the successor's S2 layering is forced by P9. P9 discusses the two objections in adjacent sentences and does not itself italicize their difference in direction. I am not claiming that the E009 criticism's repairs are wrong or unhelpful; I am claiming they address the arithmetic side and not the correspondence side or the downstream-resolution side. I am not claiming that the construct's central split was false, only that its classification of the second half was left ambiguous in a way the criticism correctly identifies.

The proposed successor artifact is the re-classification S1, the layering S2, the preservations S3, and the open question S4, expressed in prose above. It is not installed in the frozen carrier. It is a separate proposed object.

history.text:
The next inquiry warranted here is not another round of re-classification or a further sharpening of S2. It is a question about the successor's own central move: whether "source assumption" in P7 is a target at all, or only a slot in a list that the construct, the criticism, and the successor have all treated as a target because each needed somewhere to put the correspondence side.

The original occurrence that makes this relevant is P7's list itself, in the frozen excerpt:

> "One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful."

The successor reads the last item as the natural home for the correspondence side, on the strength of the observation that "the assumption that…" is a level of abstraction distinct from records, histories, and aggregates. But P7 does not say "source assumptions" in general. It says "the assumption that logical time is meaningful," which is one specific presupposition and not a category. The successor's S1 generalizes from one named member of the list to a slot it calls "source assumption," and then relocates the correspondence side there. The criticism made the same generalization in its final paragraph, calling capacity-as-sole-constraint "the natural home for 'the assumption that capacity is the only shared constraint.'" Neither the construct nor the criticism nor the successor has asked whether P7's list is meant to enumerate *kinds of target* or *examples of targets*, with the last item shown by example rather than by category.

This matters because the successor's answer to the guiding question turns on the re-classification. Under S1, the compatibility objection "changes which claim is being made, not how the arithmetic is done," and the correspondence side sits in a P7-recognized slot. If the last item of P7's list is an example rather than a category, then the correspondence side is not obviously placed by P7 at all; the successor has, in effect, extended P7's list while presenting itself as locating a slot P7 already supplies.
